nodes.outcome: Distinguish the anatomical divisions of the pituitary gland into adenohypophysis (pars distalis, pars intermedia) and neurohypophysis (pars nervosa) and explain the hypophysial portal circulation

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Hormones of Pars Distalis and Pars Intermedia
nodes.outcome: List the target organs and primary functions of GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, LH, FSH, and MSH secreted by the adenohypophysis

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Hormones of Neurohypophysis
nodes.outcome: Explain the storage, release, and physiological roles of oxytocin and vasopressin (ADH) by the neurohypophysis

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Pineal Gland and Melatonin Action
nodes.outcome: Describe the location of the pineal gland on the dorsal side of the forebrain and explain the role of melatonin in maintaining the 24-hour diurnal rhythm

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Thyroid Gland Structure and Functions of Thyroxine
nodes.outcome: Describe the bilobed follicular structure of the thyroid gland and list the physiological actions of tetraiodothyronine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3) on basal metabolic rate, erythropoiesis, and carbohydrate-protein-fat metabolism

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Hypothyroidism and Hyperthyroidism Disorders
nodes.outcome: Compare the clinical manifestations of hypothyroidism (simple goitre, cretinism, myxedema) with hyperthyroidism (Graves' disease / exophthalmic goitre)

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Antagonistic Regulation of Calcium by PTH and TCT
nodes.outcome: Explain how parathyroid hormone (PTH) and thyrocalcitonin (TCT) act antagonistically to regulate blood calcium levels through bone resorption, renal reabsorption, and intestinal absorption

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Thymus Gland, Thymosins, and Age-Related Decline
nodes.outcome: Describe the location of the thymus, the role of thymosins in T-cell differentiation and antibody production, and explain why immunity weakens in old age due to thymus degeneration

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Adrenal Medulla and Emergency Hormones
nodes.outcome: Explain the emergency fight-or-flight physiological responses induced by adrenaline and noradrenaline (catecholamines) during stress

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Adrenal Cortex Layers and Hormones
nodes.outcome: Differentiate the three layers of the adrenal cortex (zona glomerulosa, fasciculata, reticularis) and state the physiological roles of mineralocorticoids (aldosterone) and glucocorticoids (cortisol)

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Islets of Langerhans and Hormonal Secretion
nodes.outcome: Identify the pancreas as a heterocrine gland and distinguish alpha cells (secreting glucagon) from beta cells (secreting insulin) within the Islets of Langerhans

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Regulation of Blood Glucose by Insulin and Glucagon
nodes.outcome: Explain the opposing actions of insulin (glycogenesis, cellular glucose uptake) and glucagon (glycogenolysis, gluconeogenesis) in maintaining blood glucose homeostasis

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Pathophysiology and Symptoms of Diabetes Mellitus
nodes.outcome: Predict the metabolic consequences of prolonged hyperglycemia in Diabetes Mellitus, including glycosuria and ketone body formation

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Endocrine Role of Leydig Cells and Testosterone
nodes.outcome: Identify Leydig cells as the source of androgens and state the actions of testosterone in spermatogenesis, male secondary sexual characters, and libido

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Ovarian Hormones: Estrogen and Progesterone
nodes.outcome: Compare the cellular sources and physiological roles of estrogen (developing ovarian follicles) and progesterone (corpus luteum) in the female reproductive cycle and pregnancy

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Hormones of Non-Endocrine Organs: Heart and Kidney
nodes.outcome: State the triggers and functions of Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF) secreted by atrial walls and Erythropoietin (EPO) secreted by juxtaglomerular cells

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Gastrointestinal Tract Hormones
nodes.outcome: Classify the four major peptide hormones of the GI tract (gastrin, secretin, CCK, and GIP) by their target organs and physiological effects

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Chemical Classification of Hormones
nodes.outcome: Classify hormones into peptide/protein hormones, steroids, iodothyronines, and amino acid derivatives based on their chemical nature

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Mechanism of Action of Water-Soluble Hormones
nodes.outcome: Trace the mechanism of membrane-bound receptor signaling by peptide hormones involving generation of second messengers such as cAMP, IP3, and Ca2+

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Mechanism of Action of Lipid-Soluble Hormones
nodes.outcome: Trace the mechanism of intracellular/nuclear receptor binding by lipid-soluble steroid and iodothyronine hormones leading to regulation of gene expression and protein synthesis

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Comparison of Membrane vs Intracellular Receptor Mechanisms
nodes.outcome: Compare the response time, receptor location, and biochemical pathways of water-soluble versus lipid-soluble hormones

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Notochord Origin and Structure
nodes.outcome: State that the notochord is a mesodermally derived, rod-like supporting structure formed on the dorsal side during embryonic development

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Dorsal Position of Notochord
nodes.outcome: Identify the anatomical position of the notochord as running along the dorsal midline between the digestive tract and the central nervous system

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Classify Chordates and Non-chordates
nodes.outcome: Classify animals into chordates and non-chordates based on the presence or absence of a notochord at any stage of life

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Identify Non-chordate Phyla
nodes.outcome: Identify all animal phyla from Porifera to Hemichordata as non-chordates due to the complete absence of a notochord

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Seed Definition and Origin
nodes.outcome: Define a seed as a mature, fertilized ovule consisting of a seed coat and an embryo

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Basic Components of a Seed
nodes.outcome: Identify the basic components of a seed as the protective seed coat and the enclosed embryo comprising an embryonal axis and cotyledons

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Role of the Endosperm
nodes.outcome: Describe the endosperm as a food-storing tissue formed as a result of double fertilization in angiosperm seeds

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Endospermous vs Non-Endospermous Seeds
nodes.outcome: Differentiate endospermous (albuminous) seeds from non-endospermous (exalbuminous) seeds based on the persistence or complete consumption of the endosperm, citing examples like castor, pea, and bean

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: ATP as Cellular Energy Currency
nodes.outcome: Identify adenosine triphosphate (ATP) as the universal chemical energy currency in living systems

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Energy Coupling via ATP
nodes.outcome: Explain how energy released during catabolic pathways is trapped in ATP to drive anabolic processes

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Energy Extraction in Glycolysis
nodes.outcome: Identify the 10-step catabolic conversion of glucose to lactic acid or pyruvic acid as an energy-releasing pathway yielding ATP

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Metabolic Energy for Biological Work
nodes.outcome: Describe how energy derived from metabolic pathways powers cellular and physiological work such as biosynthesis and mechanical movement

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Physical vs Chemical Transformations
nodes.outcome: Distinguish between a physical change and a chemical reaction by identifying whether bonds are broken and new bonds are formed.

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Defining Rate of Chemical Reaction
nodes.outcome: State the rate of a chemical or metabolic reaction as the amount of product formed per unit time (rate = delta P / delta t).

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Temperature Coefficient (Q10 Rule)
nodes.outcome: Apply the general rule of thumb that reaction rate doubles or halves for every 10 degree Celsius change in temperature in either direction.

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Comparing Uncatalyzed and Catalyzed Rates
nodes.outcome: Calculate and compare the rate enhancement of an enzymatic reaction over an uncatalyzed reaction, such as carbonic anhydrase producing carbonic acid.

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Biosynthetic Phase Definition
nodes.outcome: Define the dark reaction (biosynthetic phase) as the enzymatic process in the stroma that uses ATP and NADPH from light reactions to fix CO2 into sugars.

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Discovery of the First CO2 Fixation Product
nodes.outcome: Identify 3-phosphoglyceric acid (PGA) as the first stable CO2 fixation product identified by Melvin Calvin using radioactive 14C in algal photosynthesis.

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Primary CO2 Acceptor in C3 Pathway
nodes.outcome: Identify ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate (RuBP), a 5-carbon ketose sugar, as the primary CO2 acceptor molecule in the C3 pathway.

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Primary CO2 Acceptor in C4 Pathway
nodes.outcome: Identify phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP), a 3-carbon compound, as the primary CO2 acceptor that forms the 4-carbon oxaloacetic acid (OAA) in C4 plants.

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Definition of Plant Growth Regulators
nodes.outcome: Define plant growth regulators (PGRs) as small, simple molecules of diverse chemical composition that regulate plant growth and development

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Five Major Classes of PGRs
nodes.outcome: List the five major groups of plant growth regulators: auxins, gibberellins, cytokinins, abscisic acid, and ethylene

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Growth Promoters vs Growth Inhibitors
nodes.outcome: Categorize the five major plant hormones into plant growth promoters (auxins, gibberellins, cytokinins) and plant growth inhibitors (abscisic acid, ethylene)

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Chemical Nature of Plant Hormones
nodes.outcome: Match each major plant hormone to its chemical nature, including indole derivatives, adenine derivatives, terpenes, carotenoid derivatives, and gases

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Blood as Gas Transport Medium
nodes.outcome: Identify blood as the common transport medium for both oxygen and carbon dioxide between the respiratory surface and tissues

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Compare O2 and CO2 Transport Modes
nodes.outcome: Compare the percentage distributions of oxygen and carbon dioxide transported in dissolved form versus erythrocyte-bound forms

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Tissue-Level Gas Exchange Dynamics
nodes.outcome: Trace the simultaneous unloading of O2 and uptake of CO2 by blood capillaries at the systemic tissue level

nodes.subject: Biology
nodes.title: Alveolar-Level Gas Exchange Dynamics
nodes.outcome: Trace the simultaneous loading of O2 onto hemoglobin and release of CO2 from carbamino-hemoglobin and bicarbonate at the alveolar capillaries
